key_insight: A practical, policy-aware framework that measures the quality of moderation decisions from humans and LLMs by balancing cost, scale, and trustworthiness, enabling continuous, auditable evaluation tied to evolving safety policies.
problem_solved: Evaluates moderation decision quality at production scale while addressing trade-offs between annotation cost, coverage, and trust (consensus/adjudication) and coping with changing policies and mixed human/LLM decision sources.
method: Policy-aligned taxonomy and labeling guidelines that map content policies to graded decision categories for consistent ground truth.
Hybrid sampling and annotation pipeline: stratified sampling for coverage, human adjudication for high-risk cases, and LLM-assisted annotations to expand scale while retaining human oversight.
Multi-dimensional metrics and feedback loop: accuracy, calibration, disagreement/consistency, and impact-weighted error rates reported in dashboards and fed back into training and policy updates.
impact: Provides a reproducible, scalable approach for auditing and improving moderation systems, helping AI/ML teams make informed deployment and retraining decisions while reducing safety and compliance risk.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: incoming content → stratified sampler → human + LLM annotation → adjudication → metric computation → feedback to models/policies
Trade-off triangle showing Cost vs Scale vs Trustworthiness with markers for different annotation strategies
Dashboard mockup with multi-dimensional metrics (accuracy, calibration, disagreement, impact-weighted errors) and time-series for trend tracking
Confusion-matrix / error heatmap annotated by policy class to highlight high-risk failure modes
paper_title: Decision Quality Evaluation Framework at Pinterest
paper_authors: Yuqi Tian, Robert Paine, Attila Dobi, Kevin O'Sullivan, Aravindh Manickavasagam
